Hi Lena — thanks for the signal and projection. I pulled together a short options-based recommendation and attached a capacity projection workbook (nova_q4_q1_capacity_projection.xlsx). High level (quick read):

- Baseline: keep current 8x A100 dedicated pool (status quo).
- Option A (expected): add 12 A100s -> 20x A100s total. This covers ~3x QPS with 99.9% of requests p95 < 300ms under sustained load and provides a 20% headroom for traffic bursts with prefix caching.
- Option B (cost-efficient): migrate to a 14x H100-equivalent cluster (or mixed A100/H100) — higher per-GPU throughput, fewer GPUs needed, better latency under long-context workloads. Equivalent performance to Option A but ~12–18% higher unit price; 14 H100s ~ recommended if you want smaller reserved footprint.
- Autoscale: include 4x burst capacity GPUs for 15-minute windows (pre-warmed) to handle unexpected spikes during launches.

Attached is the quick math and assumptions. If procurement prefers a firm throughput SLA we can offer: 350 QPS sustained with 15-minute burst to 500 QPS, backed by a 99.9% availability and p95 latency target on the primary model family (model ids in workbook).

If that sounds reasonable I’ll loop in CS (Monica) and Solutions (Rishi) to finalize the MOP & pricing.

Quick technical notes and assumptions (summary):

Assumptions we used for projection workbook:
- Current observed: 120 QPS; avg tokens/request = 400 (input + output).
- Projected (Q1): 360 QPS; avg tokens/request = 600.
- Model family: redwood-chat-3-large-ish (decoder-only style, similar perf profile to 30B class).

Throughput per GPU (observed in our infra):
- A100 (fp16, quantized kernels, batching): ~8,000 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for gen-heavy workloads at 2k context (varies with batch size).
- H100 (optimized kernels + larger memory): ~16,000 tokens/sec per GPU.

Sizing math (projected tokens/sec = QPS * tokens/request):
- Projected tokens/sec = 360 * 600 = 216,000 tokens/sec.
- Required A100s = ceil(216,000 / 8,000) = 27 -> recommend 28 A100s to leave ~3% buffer for model variability and infra noise.
- Required H100s = ceil(216,000 / 16,000) = 14 -> recommend 14 H100s.

Operational recommendations:
- Reserved pool: recommend committing to 28x A100 OR 14x H100-equivalent for the primary pool.
- Burst pool: 4 hot GPUs (H100 preferred) with pre-warmed KV cache and warm containers; auto-fallback to a compatible smaller model if capacity is exhausted.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching on high-volume flows to reduce tokens/sec by ~8–12% (already conservative in our numbers).
- Quantization: recommend int8 quant for read-heavy queries where quality is acceptable; reduces token compute and may allow 12–18% fewer GPUs.

I'll attach the micro-bench numbers in the workbook. Happy to walk through the tradeoffs on a quick call.

— Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ops warning: calling out that if they opt for A100-only, they'll need ~28 GPUs and some work to reduce cold-start tail latency for long contexts. H100 reduces overall device count but changes pricing.

Hi Lena / Rajiv / Nova procurement team — thanks for the context and patience. Below is our recommended renewal amendment and immediate next steps.

Recommended configuration (single preferred option):
- Commit: 14x H100-equivalent dedicated GPUs (primary reserved pool).
- Burst: 4x pre-warmed H100s for 15-minute bursts (hot pool).
- SLA: 350 QPS sustained on the committed model family, 15-min burst to 500 QPS, 99.9% availability, p95 latency target < 350ms for interactive flows (MOP attached).
- Term: 12-month initial commitment with an option to convert to a 24-month at a stepped discount.

Rationale: H100s give you a smaller physical footprint, improved p95 latency for long-context generations, and lower operational tail risk. Per Rishi's sizing we estimate this covers projected Q1 demand with ~7–10% headroom plus the burst pool. If Nova prefers capital-smoother spend, Option 1 (28 A100s) is also viable and included in the amendment.

Attachments: capacity workbook, MOP, pricing summary. DocuSign link for the amendment: https://redwood.app/docusign/NS-REQ-11-2026

Requested next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm preferred option (H100 or A100) and the billing account to attach the amendment.
2) Nova engineering: confirm expected model family and any upcoming feature launches that could change tokens/request assumptions.
3) We will schedule a 30-minute kick-off on acceptance to align on runbook and timeline (suggest: 11/17).

If you confirm by EOD 11/12 we can lock pricing and start provisioning to meet a 12/15 effective date.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on the next phase.
